scopes.application_note: Identification made by the paper, not a Lean hypothesis. The Lean statements quantify over arbitrary real functions R0, R1, dR1, U, V, Vx on ℝ and real numbers B, C, M, K, N; none of them mentions the paper's remainder. Applying them to the revision's text means reading R0 as R_4^(0), R1 as R_4^(1), dR1 (or deriv R1) as d_x R_4^(1), U, V, Vx as u~, v~, v~_x at a fixed time t (Lean does not require Vx to be the derivative of V), so that the integrand R0 + dR1 is the remainder R_4 = R_4^(0) + d_x R_4^(1) of (2.21) by the decomposition stated in the revision (compact TeX line 1309), and k as the mode index of (2.22). Likewise the size bound with N = ||u||_{l^1} (or ||u~||_{X_theta}) and a constant K comes from the paper's X_theta embeddings, X_theta in C^1([0,L]) for 3/4 < theta < 1 and X_theta in l^1 for cosine coefficients, and ||v~||_{C^1} <= C||u~||_{L^infty} <= C||u||_{l^1} (compact TeX lines 1315 and 1579); Lean takes the resulting pointwise inequality as a hypothesis and proves no embedding. 0 < L is the paper's standing assumption on the domain (0, L).
